paths.description: Homepage: lead-news discovery, consent entry state, global navigation, performance and security surface. Represents the main landing template.
Current article: core reading journey, article metadata, server rendering and shareability.
City weather: high-value utility template under mobile conditions.
Area selection: representative interactive personalization/search surface.
Invalid URL: recovery and not-found-state journey.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is byte-identical to the light capture and the CSS preference probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text colors.

findings.summary: Contrast is insufficient in key UI
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed color-contrast and the focused-control probe found no visible outlines on sampled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG contrast and preserve controls under prefers-contrast/forced-colors.

findings.summary: Route changes are abrupt
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no View Transition declarations while primary navigation is cross-document.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Page chrome does not communicate scroll state
findings.evidence: The long homepage has static navigation and the preference/CSS probe found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight scroll-position cue or progress treatment where it helps orientation.

findings.summary: Consent wall obscures all content on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a modal consent wall covering the news; on mobile its content is clipped horizontally.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, localized, accessible consent surface that keeps core news readable.

findings.summary: Consent UI creates duplicate document structure
findings.evidence: The area probe reports consent controls plus multiple injected h1 elements and dialogs in the page structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one correctly labelled dialog with inert background, focus management and semantic actions.

findings.summary: Dense chrome competes with news content
findings.evidence: The first viewport is dominated by two navigation rows and the consent layer; the homepage exposes 100 images and many competing sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent navigation and defer secondary modules so the lead story remains dominant.

findings.summary: Mobile layout renders at desktop width
findings.evidence: At viewport 360x800, layout measured scrollWidth 1241 and 881 px horizontal overflow; the consent dialog is visibly clipped.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix viewport sizing and replace fixed widths with intrinsic/fluid layout; test every template at 360px.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available width
findings.evidence: The 360px evidence retains a 1241px layout and the CSS probe found no container-query rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reused cards, navigation and consent controls.

findings.summary: Focus and target affordances are weak
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline none on sampled links/buttons and a visible search button measured only 16x16 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide strong :focus-visible styles and at least 44x44 CSS-pixel touch targets.

findings.summary: Consent interrupts the primary reading journey
findings.evidence: Every fresh-path screenshot opens behind the consent wall, requiring a detour before reading an article or forecast.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow immediate access to essential content and keep consent choices proportionate.

findings.summary: Loading performance misses the modern baseline
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.2s, FCP 4.1s, TBT 450ms and performance 0.50; trace LCP was 3.03s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the lead content and reduce blocking/third-party work to reach good CWV.

findings.summary: Main-thread work delays interactivity
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded 3.4s main-thread work, 1.5s JS execution, 450ms TBT and 29s time to interactive.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up work, defer nonessential scripts, and load advertising after core content.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is excessively complex
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 218 requests and 3.28MB, including 49 font requests; Lighthouse found render-blocking requests with 880ms savings and weak cache lifetimes.
findings.suggestedFix: Trim font families/weights, shorten critical chains and set effective cache policy.

findings.summary: Large unused bundles ship on first load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 644KiB unused JavaScript and 84KiB unused CSS; HAR recorded 46 script requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by template and defer ad/analytics bundles until needed or consented.

findings.summary: Some links and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-name; the image primitive found 54 images without alt and the homepage H1 is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every functional image/link an accessible name and keep decorative images explicitly alt="".

findings.summary: Text contrast fails automated testing
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed its color-contrast audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Update color tokens to meet WCAG AA across default, hover, focus and disabled states.

findings.summary: Heading and keyboard-focus structure is unreliable
findings.evidence: The homepage has an empty H1, consent injection adds multiple H1s, and sampled focused controls retained outline none.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one meaningful H1 per page and implement visible, ordered keyboard focus.

findings.summary: Mobile text is clipped outside the viewport
findings.evidence: The 360px screenshot cuts off consent copy and controls because the document remains 1241px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow copy and controls within the visual viewport with readable line lengths.

findings.summary: Reflow and target sizing fail on mobile
findings.evidence: Layout has 881px overflow at 360px and a search control measured 16x16px.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure 320/360px reflow without two-dimensional scrolling and enlarge targets.

findings.summary: Browser errors are logged
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve first-party exceptions and failed integrations, and suppress neither actionable errors nor source maps.

findings.summary: Document semantics and image assets need cleanup
findings.evidence: Doctype/UTF-8 are valid, but the main H1 is empty and image inspection found 54 missing alt attributes and 29 images without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Repair heading semantics and standardize responsive image markup.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser lifecycle blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a deprecated API, Inspector issues and five BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and address BFCache/DevTools issues.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP posture is weak
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS/nosniff are present, but CSP is missing and all 15 observed cookies were flagged insecure; many use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP and mark HTTPS cookies Secure with the narrowest suitable SameSite scope.

findings.summary: Tracking footprint is disproportionate
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 67 third-party origins and 15 known tracker domains; HAR recorded 218 requests before a consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Load only essential resources before consent and consolidate/minimize advertising and analytics vendors.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff and SAMEORIGIN, but lack CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP/frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Most core article content is absent without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 20% raw-content coverage on home and 18% on the article; the raw article lacked its title and H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render article headlines/body and core navigation, then enhance with JavaScript.

findings.summary: Top-layer consent UI breaks at narrow widths
findings.evidence: The mobile screenshot clips the modal and layout reports 881px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Constrain top-layer UI to the visual viewport and test edge/fallback positions.

findings.summary: Manifest and service worker do not provide an installable app presentation
findings.evidence: A service worker and manifest exist, but manifest display is browser and no offline fallback was exposed by the inspected configuration.
findings.suggestedFix: If app-like use is intended, provide an installable display mode and a useful offline news shell/fallback.

findings.summary: Consent design pressures acceptance before reading
findings.evidence: The blocking consent wall foregrounds Consent and delays access to public-interest news; mobile content is unreadable behind it.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally clear accept/reject controls without blocking core reading and localize the explanation.

findings.summary: Asset delivery is not consistently optimized
findings.evidence: Image evidence found 29 images without srcset and 79 below-fold images not marked lazy; Lighthouse estimated image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive modern image sources and native lazy loading below the fold.

findings.summary: Substantial background/vendor work runs on entry
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 218 requests, 46 scripts and 67 XHR/fetch requests; Lighthouse measured 3.4s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize or eliminate nonessential background fetches and advertising work.

findings.summary: Third-party and font budgets are excessive
findings.evidence: The page contacted 67 third-party origins and downloaded 49 font resources within a 3.28MB transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Set strict third-party/font budgets and defer vendors until user value or consent requires them.

findings.summary: News content is difficult for permitted agents to consume
findings.evidence: Article raw-HTML coverage is 18%, while robots explicitly disallows ChatGPT-User, GPTBot, CCBot, Google-Extended and PerplexityBot.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent discovery is desired, publish complete server-rendered article content and an explicit machine-use policy/feed.

findings.summary: No privacy-preserving on-device summary affordance is exposed
findings.evidence: Capabilities probe found no built-in AI surface on a long-form news product where optional local summarization could add value.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider an optional on-device summarizer with clear user control; do not gate core content on it.

findings.summary: Initial memory footprint is high for a news landing page
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary reported 794,000 nodes and 45.9MB self size before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendor scripts, DOM duplication and retained ad/CMP state; establish a memory budget.
